3.70.d:
सर्वभूतान्तरस्थोऽपि कर्मभिर्न च लिप्यसे ॥
अशरीरः शरीरस्थः सर्वभूतेष्ववस्थितः ॥ 7 ॥
पुरुषस्त्वं त्वमव्यक्तस्त्वमात्मा बुद्धिरेव च ॥
महाभूतानि भगवस्त्वं तथैवेन्द्रियाणि च ॥ 8 ॥
योगिभिर्मृष्यसे योगज्ञानज्ञेयपुरातन ॥
ये त्वां भजन्ति ते यान्ति भगवन्परमां गतिम् ॥ 9 ॥
जयमनघमजेयं विश्वगं देवदेवं त्रिदशरिपुविनाशे नित्यमुद्युक्तशक्तिम् ॥
द्विजसुरवरवन्द्यं नाशनं कल्मषाणां शरणमुपगतोऽहं वासुदेवं शरण्यम् ॥ 3.347.10 ॥
3.348
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
वसुना वसुवेशेन वाग्मिना विष्णुरीडितः ॥
उवाच प्राञ्जलिं प्रह्वं पार्थिवं पुरतः स्थितम्॥1॥
वासुदेव उवाच ॥
नानृतं नृप वक्तव्यं प्राणैः कण्ठगतैरपि ॥
धर्मप्रश्नो न वक्तव्यस्तथैकेन विशेषतः ॥ 2 ॥
3.70.m:
Although dwelling within all beings, you are not stained by actions; / bodiless, yet dwelling in the body, remaining in all beings.
You are the Puruṣa, you are the Unmanifest, you are the Self and the intellect; / you are the great elements, O Blessed One, and likewise the senses.
You are meditated upon by yogins, O ancient one who are to be known by the knowledge of yoga; / those who worship you, O Blessed One, attain the supreme state.
I have taken refuge in Vāsudeva, the worthy refuge: victorious, sinless, invincible, omnipresent, the God of gods, / whose power is ever ready to destroy the enemies of the thirty [gods], / worshipful by the best of twice-born and gods, the destroyer of sins.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Praised by Vasu, clad in radiant form and eloquent, Viṣṇu / spoke to the king who stood before him, bowed with folded hands:
Vāsudeva said: / An untruth should not be spoken, O king, even when the breaths have reached the throat; / likewise, a question on dharma especially should not be answered by one alone.

3.70.d:
बहुज्ञेनापि धर्मज्ञ धर्मकामेन कर्हिचित् ॥
दुर्विज्ञेयास्तथा धर्माः सूक्ष्मा राजन्दुरन्वयाः ॥ 3 ॥
तस्मान्नैकेन वक्तव्याः कदाचिदपि जानता ॥
उक्तानृतं महत्प्राप्तं त्वया कृच्छ्रं नराधिप ॥ 4 ॥
गतिभ्रंशस्तथैवाप्ता देवयज्ञार्थवादिना ॥
मम भक्तोऽसि सततं तेन ते निष्कृतिः कृता॥5॥
कालेनाल्पेन कल्पेन या न शक्या सुरासुरैः ॥
गच्छ पालय राज्यं त्वं तथैवाविचलो भव ॥ 6 ॥
नावमानं त्वया कार्यं ब्राह्मणानां कथञ्चन ॥
ब्राह्मणो हि महद्भूतं विज्ञेयं दैवतं परम् ॥ 7 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्त्वा वसुं विष्णुस्तत्रैवादर्शनं गतः ॥
तार्क्ष्येण सहितो राजन्विस्मितश्चाभवद्वसुः॥8॥
राज्यं चावाप भूयोऽपि खेचरत्वं तथैव च॥
ततः सभाजितश्चापि देवैः सर्वैः समागतैः ॥ 9 ॥
3.70.m:
even by one who knows much, O knower of dharma, who desires dharma at any time. / For duties are difficult to discern, subtle, O king, and hard to trace.
Therefore, it should never be spoken by one alone who knows. / Having spoken an untruth, a great hardship has been incurred by you, O ruler of men.
A fall from your station was likewise incurred by speaking for the sake of the gods' sacrifice; / you are continually my devotee, and on that account expiation has been made for you.
In a short time, which was not capable [of being attained] by gods and asuras even in an aeon. / Go, protect your kingdom, and remain likewise unwavering.
Disrespect toward brahmins must never be shown by you in any way; / for a brahmin is a great being, to be known as the supreme deity.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Having spoken thus to Vasu, Viṣṇu vanished right there / along with Garuḍa, O king; and Vasu was filled with wonder.
He also regained his kingdom once more, and likewise the ability to move through the sky; / then he was greeted with respect by all the gods assembled together.

3.349
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥ ॥
विश्वरूपं समाचक्ष्व देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
कस्य तूद्दर्शितं तेन भृगुवंशविवर्धन ॥ 1 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एकान्तभावनाभक्तैर्दृष्टानि बहुशः पुरा ॥
विश्वरूपाणि देवस्य यान्यशक्यानि भाषितुम् ॥ 2 ॥
वासुदेवप्रसादेन न भवेद्दिव्यदर्शनः ॥
विश्वरूपधरं द्रष्टुं तावच्छक्तिर्न विद्यते ॥ 3॥
तत्र यद्दर्शितं चैव नारदस्य पुरानघ ॥
तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि विश्वदेवेन विष्णुना ॥ 4 ॥
नारदः सुमहद्भूतं नरनारायणाश्रयम् ॥
बदर्याश्रममित्युक्तं जगामातिमनोहरम् ॥ 5 ॥
चतुरात्मा हरिर्यत्र धर्मपुत्रत्वमागतः॥
हरिः कृष्णो नरश्चैव तथा नारायणः प्रभुः ॥ 6 ॥
3.70.m:
Thus ends the three hundred and forty-eighth chapter, named 'The Narrative of Vasu', in the third book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Vajra said: / Describe the universal form of the God of gods who bears the discus; / to whom was it shown by him, O enhancer of the Bhṛgu lineage?
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / By devotees with exclusive devotion the universal forms of the God, / which are impossible to describe, were seen many times of old.
Without the grace of Vāsudeva, one does not become endowed with divine vision; / until then there is no capacity to see him bearing the universal form.
In that regard, that which was shown of old to Nārada, O sinless one, / by Viṣṇu, the God of all, that I shall declare to you.
Nārada went to Badaryāśrama, very wonderful, / the abode of Nara-Nārāyaṇa, celebrated as exceedingly delightful,
where Hari, fourfold in self, assumed the state of being the sons of Dharma: / Hari, Kṛṣṇa, Nara, and Lord Nārāyaṇa.

3.70.m:
At that time, Hari Kṛṣṇa, when he had passed, was indeed in another world; / and the gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa were likewise devoted to severe austerity.
Stationed on an eight-wheeled vehicle, full of splendour and charming, / standing on one foot, without support, both with arms raised aloft.
Nārada saw both of them there, of blazing splendour; / having saluted the two departed gods, he stood before them.
The twice-born, having then been honoured by Nara and Nārāyaṇa / with water for the feet, respectful offering, water for sipping, and the like, resided there in their hermitage.
Dwelling in the hermitage, that best of vipras once saw the two best of gods, / the sinless ones, performing divine rites without obstacle.
Then, having performed his daily rites, Nārada spoke to those two teachers of the world: / “You two are the lords of the worlds, you two are the supreme lords.
For whose propitiation are you both here engaged in austerity? / Who is worshipped by you two and intended in rites to gods and ancestors?"

3.70.m:
["The two said:] / Our supreme Prakṛti, from whom is the origin of all, / in order to show the proper norm, we ever worship that new, undefeated [Lord],
O brahman, in rites intended for gods and ancestors. / In the three worlds, vipras, divine gurus, cows, and the ancestors—
those who worship them, worship indeed that God, the supreme Lord; / whoever worships a god, by him Hari is worshipped.
Even if devoid of rules, O fortunate one, because he is all-pervading; / and desiring to make worship of another god, one should worship Hari.
by that, worship of him is performed according to the prescribed rite, O best of the twice-born; / for the gods and all that is contained in the three worlds reside in the God.
Worship of the three worlds is performed by one who performs the worship of Viṣṇu. / There is no such Brahman in the worlds where Janārdana is not present;
nor is there anything in the worlds that is not established in Viṣṇu: / in whom is all, from whom is all, who is all, and who is everywhere,

यश्च सर्वमयो नित्यं तस्मै सर्वात्मने नमः ॥
क्षीरोद मध्ये द्वीपोऽस्ति बहुयोजनविस्तृतः ॥21॥
तत्र ते पुरुषाः श्वेताः शशाङ्कसमतेजसः ॥
उपेताश्च तथा सर्वे चक्रवर्त्युपलक्षणैः ॥ 22॥
पञ्चरात्रविधानज्ञाः पूजयन्ति सदा हरिम् ॥
मायादेहमथास्थाय देवोऽपि मधुसूदनः ॥23॥
तत्पूजां प्रतिगृह्णाति शिरसा सततं हरिः ॥
तैस्सार्धं रमते नित्यं तैश्च संपूज्यते सदा ॥24॥
एकान्तभावोपगता ये भवन्तीह मानवाः ॥
अकामाश्च जगन्नाथमर्चयन्ति सदा च ये ॥ 25 ॥
ते यान्ति देहमुत्सृज्य तद्द्वीपं श्वेतसंज्ञितम् ॥
अनिष्यन्दा निराहाराः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः॥26॥
सर्वेश्वरा नित्यतृप्ताः परं सुखमुपागताः ॥
पूजयन्ति हरिं तत्र दिव्यं वर्षशतं पुनः ॥27॥
ततोऽर्कमण्डलं भित्त्वा अनिरुद्धं विशन्ति ते ॥
ब्रह्मम्̐स्तपोभिः प्रद्युम्नं ततः संकर्षणं प्रभुम्॥28॥
3.70.m:
and who is eternally composed of all—homage to him, the Self of all! / In the middle of the Kṣīroda ocean there is an island extending many yojanas.
There the men are white, of splendour equal to the moon, / and all are endowed with the marks of universal emperors.
Knowing the prescribed rite of the Pañcarātra, they ever worship Hari. / Moreover, assuming an illusory body, the god Madhusūdana too—"
Hari continually receives that worship with his head; / he always delights with them, and is ever worshipped by them.
Those men here who are endowed with exclusive devotion, / and who, devoid of desire, ever worship the lord of the world,
having abandoned the body, they go to that island called Śveta, / free from exudation, taking no food, all-knowing, and seeing everything.
Lords of all, eternally contented, having attained supreme bliss, / they worship Hari there again for a hundred divine years.
Then, piercing the solar orb, they enter Aniruddha, / through austerities, O sage, into Pradyumna, and then into the lord Saṃkarṣaṇa.

भवन्ति सर्वे सर्वत्र सर्वदा सर्वशक्तयः ॥ 29 ॥

स त्वं शीघ्रमितो गत्वा श्वेतद्वीपनिवासिनः॥.3.349.30॥
पश्य त्वं पुरुषान्ब्रह्मन्प्रसन्नः स विभुस्तव ॥

तं तु देशं गता ब्रह्मन्न तैर्दृष्टो जनार्दनः ॥

जितं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष नमस्ते विश्वभावन ॥
नमस्तेऽस्तु हृषीकेश महापुरुष पूर्वज ॥ 35 ॥
3.70.m:
Then, having reached Vāsudeva, they become just like him; / thereupon all become omnipotent, everywhere, at all times,
and, freed from all sufferings, they have attained supreme bliss. / So go quickly from here and [look upon] the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa.
Behold those men, O brahmin; that lord, being pleased with you, / will show [you] his wondrous form, a marvel to the three worlds,
[his] universal form, O tiger among brahmins, pleased Madhusūdana. / Ekata, Dvita, and Trita of great austerities,
having gone to that realm, O brahmin, did not see Janārdana, / because [only] those endowed with exclusive devotion [can see] the world-teacher.
They only heard the verse uttered by the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa, / the highly fortunate ones free of all taint:
“Victory to you, O Puṇḍarīkākṣa! Homage to you, creator of the universe! / May homage be to you, O Hṛṣīkeśa, supreme person, first-born!”

3.70.m:
Hearing this verse, they also heard a bodiless voice / of Hari, O highly fortunate one, bringing benefit to all beings:
“[Does anyone] meet death ever after reaching Śvetadvīpa? / There is no entry into Śvetadvīpa without being single-minded devotees, O brahmins.
You are devotees of ordinary disposition and rich in austerity; / endowed with severe austerity, you have therefore come to my land.
You whose essence is of ordinary devotion, go back without delay; / by you the persons dwelling in Śvetadvīpa have been seen.
Through these verses Janārdana is likewise seen; / by men devoted to exclusive devotion, this [verse]
It should be continually murmured, O brahmins; then you will come here again; / this verse is purifying, sacred, and the destroyer of all sins.
The knowing man must perform japa and homa with these verses and with devotion, / as well as the offering of incense, lamps, food, and flowers.

आपत्प्राप्तेन जप्तव्यं तन्मोक्षार्थं तथैव च ॥
एतस्य जापः कर्तव्यो नित्यमेव विजानता ॥ 45 ॥
एतस्य जापात्पुरुषः सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥
एतां श्रुत्वा तु ते वाणीं चागता मगधाः पुनः ॥ 46 ॥
दृष्टवन्तो वसुं तत्र यजमानं महीपतिम् ॥
याजको यस्य धर्मात्मा देवाचार्यो बृहस्पतिः ॥ 47 ॥
अदृश्येन हृतो भागस्तत्र देवेन विष्णुना ॥
जगृहुर्देवताः सर्वा दृश्यभागात्पुरोधसः ॥ 48 ॥
विष्टं प्रति गतक्रोधं देवाचार्यं बृहस्पतिम् ॥
एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैवमवोचतम् ॥ 49 ॥
3.70.m:
A wise man should recite this verse during prostration and clockwise circumambulation; / bathing should be performed with this, and at the end water [offered], O brahmins.
Removing all sins, meritorious, granting liberation, granting all desires, / this auspicious verse is declared to bestow all wishes.
It should be muttered by one fallen into misfortune, and likewise for the sake of liberation; / japa of this must be performed constantly by the knowing person.
From the japa of this, a person attains all desires.” / Having heard this voice, those [sages] returned to the Magadhas.
They saw King Vasu there acting as the patron of the sacrifice, / whose righteous officiating priest was Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods.
There, the share was taken invisibly by the god Viṣṇu; / all the [other] deities took their visible shares from the priest.
Toward Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods, whose anger had subsided toward the sacrificial seat, / Ekata, Dvita, and Trita spoke thus:

अदृश्यः सर्वदेवानां तं कथं द्रष्टुमिच्छसि ॥

समापयामास तदा तं यज्ञं पार्थिवस्य च ॥
एकान्तभावोपगता ऋषयोऽपि जनार्दनम् ॥ 51 ॥
आगता देवकार्यार्थं श्वेतद्वीपात्पुरा द्विज ॥
श्वेतद्वीपं पुनः प्राप्तं पुनरावृत्तिदुर्लभम् ॥ 52 ॥
तस्मात्तं देवदेवेशं तत्रस्थं पश्य नारद ॥
त्वयापि देवकार्याणि कर्तव्यानि बहून्यथ ॥ 53 ॥
श्वेतद्वीपगतस्यापि तेन ते द्विज साम्प्रतम् ॥
न भविष्यति लोकेषु गतिर्निर्वाणकारिणी ॥
कल्पावसाने तु गतिं तां त्वं विप्र गमिष्यसि ॥ 54 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
एवमुक्तस्ततः शीघ्रं मनोमारुतरंहसा ॥
अभिवाद्याथ तौ देवौ तं द्वीपं नारदो गतः ॥ 55 ॥
स तत्र गत्वा ददृशे श्वेतद्वीप निवासिनः ॥
पूजयामास शिरसा तांश्च भक्त्या स नारदः ॥ 56 ॥
3.70.m:
“He is invisible to all the gods; how do you wish to see him?” / Thus consoled, Bṛhaspati, the teacher of the gods,
then brought that sacrifice of the king to completion. / Even the ṛṣis endowed with exclusive devotion to Janārdana,
having come from Śvetadvīpa for divine business in ancient times, O brahmin, / reached Śvetadvīpa again, which is hard to attain for one who must return.
Therefore, see that lord of the gods who resides there, O Nārada; / for you too have many divine tasks to perform.
Even though you go to Śvetadvīpa, O brahmin, you will not at present / have in the worlds that state which brings nirvāṇa; / but at the end of the kalpa, O brahmin, you will attain that state.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Addressed thus, having saluted those two gods, Nārada then went quickly / to that island with the speed of mind and wind.
Having gone there, he saw the dwellers of Śvetadvīpa, / and Nārada worshipped them with his head, full of devotion.

3.70.m:
Having reached the great white island, Nārada, glad at heart, / saw those very men, white, with the lustre of the moon, and auspicious.
He honoured them with his head, and was mentally honoured by them; / desirous to see [the Lord], devoted to japa, regarded as enduring every hardship,
With a single-pointed mind, the brahmin, whose arms were long, raised his arms / and sang a hymn of praise to the All, the qualityless, whose self is the qualities:
to peaceful Vāsudeva, and the creator of the universe, O brahmin, / to the endless, the immeasurable, the omnipresent, exceedingly swift,
to him of boundless strength and valour, perpetually worshipped by gods and munis, / to Viṣṇu, destroyer of the burden of worldly existence, destroyer of the sins of those who bow to him.
